page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine belonging to the c4 instance family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8581C processor operating at 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators. The underlying x86_64 architecture supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512).

Benchmark data reveals a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves top-tier results in single-core metrics, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2319.0 and strong single-threaded performance in gzip compression (35.15 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.87 GB/sec). However, multi-core and memory sub-systems show limitations. The Passmark memory score is poor at 1085.12, and uncached memory read bandwidth is weak at 38.47 GB/sec. Multi-core stress-ng performance also falls into the bottom 25% tier.

Given the high single-core efficiency and hardware-accelerated matrix instructions, this instance is suited for lightweight compute-bound tasks, text processing, and basic web serving. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases or parallelized multi-threaded workloads due to memory bandwidth constraints and lower multi-core scaling. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the instance offers a dense compute profile for workloads that benefit from dedicated CPU execution without requiring large memory footprints.
